Subject: Follow-up: pilot scope & deployment preferences

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the discovery call this morning — Daniel and I found the conversation helpful. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can scope a pilot: 

Summary of Acme's needs:
- Volume: ~30–50M inference tokens/month to start (customer-facing chat + short summaries).
- Latency: p95 target ~150–250ms for chat; occasional spikes tolerable.
- Security: we need VPC/private connectivity for production; pilot can be hosted if we can validate controls.
- Uptime: production SLA expectation is 99.9% post-pilot.

Immediate asks for scoping/pricing:
1) Can you provide 2–3 pricing scenarios comparing Hosted API (per-token), Dedicated reserved capacity (monthly GPU commit), and Private VPC (both managed and on-prem outline)? We want a clear cost delta for 40M tokens/month baseline and a 3x growth case.
2) Any runbook/requirements for private connectivity (VPC peering, IP ranges, certs)?
3) Can you send a sample SOW and pilot pricing worksheet we can share with procurement?

If you can send those by early next week that would be ideal — procurement wants a ballpark before our internal prioritization meeting on Sep 24.

Thanks,
Sabrina Moore

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>

Hi team — attached is a first-pass worksheet (redwood_pilot_pricing_v1.xlsx) with three scenarios and the assumptions used. High-level notes below; see worksheet for line-item math. Attachment stub: redwood_pilot_pricing_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 54KB).

Assumptions used for 40M token baseline:
- Request mix: 70% chat (avg 50 tokens), 30% summaries (avg 350 tokens).
- Effective tokens billed = 40M.
- Peak concurrency considerations included as a headroom multiplier for Dedicated sizing.

Scenario summaries (monthly, USD, approximate):
- Hosted API (pay-as-you-go): ~ $2,400–$3,200/mo for 40M tokens (range reflects model variants and streaming vs non-streaming). Per-token rates used: $0.00006–$0.00008. Pros: fastest start, no infra lead time. Cons: higher unit cost at scale, limited control for private connectivity unless combined with VPC bridges and enterprise contract.

- Dedicated Reserved (committed GPU pool): ~ $1,500–$2,200/mo effective unit cost for same throughput (40M tokens) after amortizing reserved GPU costs with expected utilization. Assumes 1x A10-equivalent pool with autoscale burst available; 12-month commit recommended for best pricing. Pros: predictable throughput and lower unit cost at sustained use. Cons: commit required, longer procurement cycle.

- Private VPC (managed): ~ $1,800–$2,400/mo effective when including managed networking and support uplift; on-prem option adds a one-time integration/installation fee (example: $45k–$60k) and lower ongoing infra op cost depending on customer infra. Pros: meets residency and security controls, full-network isolation. Cons: higher initial setup and ops responsibility for on-prem.

3x growth case (120M tokens): the math favors Dedicated and Private — effective per-token drops by ~30–50% under steady utilization assumptions. See worksheet "ScaleImpact" tab for detailed curves.

Latency/throughput notes:
- Hosted: p95 typically within target for chat on smaller models; heavier models or longer contexts push p95 upward.
- Dedicated: can tune batch sizes and allocation to get stable p95 ~150–250ms for the request mix you described.
- Private/on-prem: dependent on customer infra and networking; we provide recommended instance types and tuning knobs in the doc.

Recommended next steps:
1) We deliver the attached XLSX + SOW draft by Tue Sep 23 (ETA preserved).
2) Schedule a 60-minute technical workshop (Redwood SE + Acme infra) to review VPC requirements and pilot acceptance criteria. Propose Wed Sep 24 or Thu Sep 25.
3) If procurement needs a formal quote for Dedicated reserved capacity, we'll prepare a 30/60/90-day commit pricing addendum.

Let me know if you want different growth scenarios modeled (e.g., caching or prefix reuse assumptions) — we can toggle those to show lower token consumption.

Cheers,
Markus Klein
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai
